subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the angle between the curves x² + 3y = 3 and x² − y² + 25 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.220, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 7(iv). Chapter 10 is printed as five un-numbered sub-sections inside one chapter box and each sub-section restarts its own numbering, so the sub-section is named here; we ship the whole chapter as ONE unit. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which variable you eliminate, which root of y you reject and why, and what formula gives the angle.

steps.label: Find the points of intersection
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Eliminate x², not y — both equations carry x² by itself, so one substitution leaves a quadratic in y. The root y = 4 must be rejected in writing, because it makes x² negative.
lines: Given curves:  x² + 3y = 3   …(i)   and   x² − y² + 25 = 0   …(ii)
If y = 4:  x² = 3 − 12 = −9, which is impossible. Reject y = 4.
∴ the curves meet at P(2√6, −7) and at (−2√6, −7). Work at P.

recall.must_convey: That eliminating x² gives y² + 3y − 28 = 0, y = −7 (rejecting y = 4), and x = ±2√6.
accept: write x squared as three minus three y and substitute
y squared plus three y minus twenty eight equals zero
y is minus seven because y equals four makes x squared negative
x square negative avutundi kabatti y equals four reject cheyyali
x squared is twenty four so x is plus or minus two root six
heard_as: y squared plus three y minus twenty eight

steps.why: Both equations contain x² and no other power of x, so eliminating x² is one substitution and leaves an ordinary quadratic. Rejecting y = 4 with a stated reason, that x² cannot be negative, is part of the method mark.
common_mistakes: Keeping y = 4 and reporting a second angle at a point that does not exist.
Sign slip in −y² − 3y + 28 = 0 when multiplying through by −1.
steps.memory_tip: When both curves show the same square term on its own, eliminate that square — it is one substitution instead of two.

steps.label: Find both slopes there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Keep the surd as 2√6 through the whole step. Turning it into a decimal here makes the cancelling in the last step impossible to see.

accept: differentiate the first curve to get minus two x by three
differentiate the second curve to get x by y
m one is minus four root six by three
surd ni decimal ga marchakunda 2 root 6 ga unchali
m two is minus two root six by seven
keep the root six as it is

steps.why: The second curve differentiates to the very simple x/y because the x² and the −y² have opposite signs and the same coefficient. Keeping the surd exact is what makes the √6 factor out cleanly in the last step.
common_mistakes: Writing the second slope as −x/y by mishandling the minus on y².
Replacing 2√6 by 4.9 and then being unable to reach an exact answer.
Differentiating 3y as 3 without the dy/dx factor.
steps.memory_tip: For x² − y² = k the slope is x/y, and for x² + y² = k it is −x/y — the sign inside the curve is the sign that flips.

steps.label: Apply the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Take the numerator over the common denominator 21 and write the denominator over 21 as well; the 21s then cancel and leave 22√6/69.

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = 22√6/69, so θ = Tan⁻¹(22√6/69), roughly 38 degrees.
accept: take a common denominator of twenty one for both parts
m one minus m two is minus twenty two root six by twenty one
one plus m one m two is sixty nine by twenty one
twenty one cancel ayyi twenty two root six by sixty nine vasthundi
the angle is tan inverse twenty two root six by sixty nine
root six times root six is six

steps.why: √6 · √6 = 6, so the product of the two slopes is a plain rational number while their difference keeps one factor of √6. That is why the surd is left only in the numerator of the final answer.
common_mistakes: Writing (√6)² as √36 or as 36 instead of 6.
Cancelling 22 against 69, which share no factor.
Forgetting the 1 in 1 + m₁m₂ and using only 48/21.
steps.memory_tip: Put both the numerator and the denominator over the same number, here 21, and that number cancels itself out.
